complexity_ledger.narrative: SM-04 fixed four defects in the eval scorecard and NOTHING ELSE, and bumped the card to `scorecard_version 3`. THE ANCHORS DID NOT MOVE: `anchors_digest` is `sha256:eeccf4576bc6fd85` at versions 1, 2 and 3 alike, `check` recomputes it from the file on every run, and a test asserts the literal. D2, D4 and D5 are all still on the card. 1. THE DIGEST WAS BLIND TO WHAT REACHED A JUDGE. `sha256:e33638087c4191da` at six commits spanning 9,705 to 19,503 bytes -- one hash over a file that doubled, every version of which the dispatch told the judges to read in full. The fix is not a wider hash: it is that "what reaches a judge" now HAS a definition. `served_rubric` renders the judge-facing rubric from parsed structure only, `serve` emits it, `scaffold` writes the same bytes into `scorecard.md`, and every card records `served_digest` over exactly those bytes. Defects 1 and 2 are one fix, because you cannot digest what reaches a judge until you have decided what reaches a judge. 2. A JUDGE WAS SERVED THE FINDING THEY WERE THE INSTRUMENT FOR. The mechanism is the whitelist -- ` later editor adds are outside the renderer by construction, so a new section does not reach a judge by default. The refusal is the backstop. It found two REAL leaks, and the second is the one nobody had seen: `FI-03-DF-02` and `FI-06-DF-04` both located the contamination in the rubric FILE, and neither looked at `_skeleton_md`, which told every version 2 judge "D1, D4 and D5 all moved on unchanged input" IN THEIR OWN CARD. 6 of 6 version 2 cards. Filed as `SM-04-DF-01`; two independent adversarial channels named the right paragraph and the wrong file. 3. D5's ANCHOR IS AMBIGUOUS AND STAYS THAT WAY, VISIBLY. The anchor is untouched. Version 3 does to it what version 2 did to practice: record the choice, never mandate it. It fired once in this round and did exactly what it says -- one judge scored 3 with `anchor_reading: measured` and wrote that under `disclosure` the same lines are a 4. The judge who did NOT reach the field found the sharper thing: the two readings only diverge once anchor 3 holds, so the rule as shipped over-collects, which is the safe direction. 4. `total` IS GONE, and the removal is PRICED rather than assumed. `removal_is_a_delta_rule`: SM-01 seeded for two cuts and neither is this one, so the gap was seeded here, both sides measured in one run. SM-04-GM-T1 -- a dimension score altered in a card, nothing else touched: BEFORE, version 2 card, SEALED:    caught twice (total arithmetic + seal) AFTER,  version 3 card, SEALED:    caught once  (seal digest) -> REDUNDANT BEFORE, version 2 card, UNSEALED:  caught once  (total arithmetic) AFTER,  version 3 card, UNSEALED:  CAUGHT BY NOTHING -> LOAD-BEARING So the cut is free on a sealed card and it is not free on an unsealed one. That is the price and it is in the test, not in prose: `test_the_price_of_removing_total_measured_on_both_sides`. THE RE-SCORE THE CHANGE RULE REQUIRES. Four fresh blind judges, one sealed artifact, two under a frozen version 2 rubric and two under version 3, same day, same dispatch. The bump: 3 points of summed |movement| over 10 judge-scores, worst 1 per judge, all on D4 and D5; D1, D2 and D3 moved zero. FI-03's bump was 4 over 30, worst 1 -- same worst case, higher per-score rate on a quarter of the sample. NOTHING HERE SAYS THE BUMP IS FREE. THE FINDING THE CORE CANNOT EXPRESS, and it is unflattering to version 2's own rationale. FI-03 explained D4 by JUDGING PRACTICE and version 2 was built on that explanation. All four judges here recorded `executed_own_faults: true`, and D4 came out 2, 3, 3, 4 -- with a -2 against FI-03's version 2 row, practice recorded true at BOTH ends. Recording the practice made the variable visible; it did not make the dimension stable. `SM-04-DF-07`. The decontamination is confounded with the round and that half is filed as a HYPOTHESIS, not a cause. AND THE ONE ABOUT D2, WHICH THIS TICKET MAY NOT TOUCH. D2 = 2 on 31 of 31 cards ever written; these four are the 28th to the 31st and the first served a card that told them nothing about how D2 has scored. All four gave anchor 3's unreachability as the reason, unprompted. A judge then found a SECOND crack: read cumulatively, D2 anchor 2 sits above anchor 0's "complexity is unmeasured", so an artifact measuring none is forced to 0 -- a 2-to-4-point spread, wider than the D5 one version 3 exists to record. Filed as `SM-04-DF-06` and NOT FIXED. Rewriting D2's anchors would pre-decide SM-05, which is the one thing this ticket was told twice not to do. A SHIPPED TRIPWIRE CAUGHT THIS TICKET AND WAS NOT FIXED BY EXEMPTION. Declaring the version bump as an instrument change made `audit` report nine SUPERSEDED-UNMARKED violations at once -- R-H3 firing on the ticket that shipped the change. All nine were answered from the raw data per the card's own straddle warning: six re-affirmed at `2098d55` (nothing measuring kills or complexity imports `score_tools` or reads the rubric -- the three files that name them do so in a docstring), two re-affirmed and widened, and one SUPERSEDED. That last is FI-03's "at most one dimension-point per judge", which was a property of two adjacent rounds rather than of the instrument, and which its own `why` had warned was the flattering half of that ticket's numbers. The change is declared with NO `affects`, applying it to every card, which leaves 22 standing OPENs -- scoping it narrower would have kept the audit quiet by narrowing a true statement, and the dilution cost is reported rather than hidden. MY OWN ROUND-CONDUCT ERROR, DISCLOSED. I read both pass-2 cards while their judges were still writing, mistook an in-progress file for an unfilled one, and messaged two judges mid-score. Both correctly refused to change anything and no score moved. Contacting a judge during scoring is the operator error this card's version 3 is about, and an operator who hides their own is not entitled to report anyone else's. It is in RESULT.md section 0. DENOMINATOR RULE. Scoring rules 8 -> 9: numerator rose, nothing removed. Card top-level fields 15 -> 14: `total` out, `served_digest`, `file_sha256` and `anchor_reading` in. Served lines carrying a result about a dimension: 1 -> 0 in the rubric, 3 -> 0 in the scaffold. Tests in `test_score_tools.py` 60 -> 72, ZERO DELETED. Suite 1359 -> 1375: +12 mine, +4 ticket-workspace tests that go away at close. Acceptance: 1375 passed in 445.75s. Parent 0342a3a: 1359 passed in 354.00s. Findings SM-04-DF-01..07 filed: five carried (budget 5, spent exactly), two repaired. NONE of the carried ones fixed.

coverage audit (MF-026) is `not_run`: audit has not been run for this scope. RECORDED, NOT REFUSED (2026-08-04). refinement.detail: SEARCHED, FOUND NONE, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE POINT. `direction=zero` against SM-02: nothing in this ticket touches modeled surface. Everything it ships lives under `references/`, `examples/validation/scorecards/`, `tests/` and `specs/results/`, none of which is in `representation_scope`. `specs/current` is byte-unchanged, exactly as `model_delta_expectation: none expected` says. THREE REFINEMENTS WERE CONSIDERED AND ALL THREE REJECTED, and the reasons matter more than the outcome. 1. FOLD THE PROSE INTO THE PARSED RUBRIC DIGEST, so any edit to `references/eval_scorecard.md` invalidates every skeleton. REJECTED, and `FI-03-DF-02` says why in its own words: the digest is RIGHT to exclude prose from the scaffold-time check, because a rubric whose every typo re-scaffolds the round is unusable, and `audit` would have gone red for a typo. What was missing was a RECORD that the file changed, not a wider hash. Shipped as `file_sha256` plus a `PROSE-DRIFT` note, which is an OPEN and never a violation. 2. MAKE `result_leaks` A CLOSE-TIME CHECK OVER FILLED CARDS. REJECTED and filed as `SM-04-DF-04`. Run over the 36 cards in the tree it reports 14, and EIGHT of those are the judge's own writing -- including a judge honestly disclosing that the rubric had contaminated them, which is the most valuable sentence in that round. A check that punishes the disclosure channel would cost more than the leak it catches. The contract is SERVED TEXT ONLY, and it is now written down. 3. BUILD A CHECKER OVER `JUDGE-DISPATCH*.md`, so a dispatch that points a judge at the rubric file is contradicted by a command rather than by a reader's memory. REJECTED and filed as `SM-04-DF-03`. It is a new instrument, R1 says an instrument ships with a demonstrated failing input, and it sits close to the standing rule's boundary -- refusing to serve a contaminated card is data hygiene, and a checker that reads a dispatch and refuses is a step toward gating how a round is run. Naming the residue is worth more than the appearance of coverage.

goals.expected_effect: none on the number itself; ensures SM-05's judges are not contaminated the way FI-03's were
goals.local_signal: serve a card to a judge and confirm the result-stating section is absent

ticket.objective: Fix what is demonstrably broken and NOTHING ELSE. The rubric digest is identical across a rubric change that changed judging behaviour, because it covers anchors only. FI-03's judges were handed a rubric section stating the result they were the instrument for, while PA-06's judges were not -- a judge must never be given the finding they are measuring. D5 splits 3 vs 4 between judges who BOTH executed, so judging_practice does not explain it and the anchor is ambiguous. `total` is still printed while four of its five terms are unstable or constant. DO NOT RETIRE D2, D4 OR D5 -- that would destroy SM-05's experiment. DO NOT tune an anchor so a number moves.
ticket.title: Harden the scorecard where it is broken, without retiring what has not been tested
